S043.name: Restrictive_Intake
S043.description: Persistent restriction of energy intake relative to requirements, leading to significantly low body weight.

subtypes.Eating Very Small Amounts: Eating only one or two bites a day or extremely small portions per meal.
subtypes.Skipping Meals: Intentionally skipping breakfast, lunch, or dinner.
subtypes.Exclusion of Specific Food Groups: Strictly avoiding specific food groups like carbohydrates or fats to prevent nutritional imbalance.
subtypes.Strict Calorie Restriction: Limiting daily caloric intake to an extremely low level.

S044.name: Low_Weight
S044.description: A body weight that is significantly below the minimum level of health for age, sex, developmental trajectory, and physical health.

subtypes.Continuous Weight Loss: A state where weight continues to decrease due to intentional restriction of intake.
subtypes.Insistence on Low Weight: Attempting to lose more weight or refusing to restore weight despite already being underweight.

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.

subtypes.Fear of Weight Gain: Extreme fear and loathing of gaining weight or becoming fat.
subtypes.Fear of Specific Foods: Fear that eating high-calorie foods will immediately lead to weight gain.
subtypes.Obsession with Weight Gain: Compulsively checking the scale and becoming extremely anxious about even the slightest increase.

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.

subtypes.Distorted Body Image: Perceiving one's body as much fatter than it actually is or perceiving specific parts as excessively large when looking in the mirror.
subtypes.Self-Worth Dependent on Weight: Judging whether one is a good or successful person solely based on weight or body shape.

S084.name: Low_Weight_Severity_Non_Recognition
S084.description: Persistent lack of recognition of the seriousness of the current low body weight.

subtypes.Denial of Medical Risk: Not admitting or dismissing the health risks caused by being underweight.
subtypes.Disregard of Symptoms: Not taking physical symptoms caused by low weight (dizziness, hair loss, amenorrhea) seriously.
subtypes.Dismissal of Concerns: Exaggerating or rejecting the concerns of doctors or family as unnecessary.

symptom.disease_info: Anorexia nervosa is defined by persistent restriction of energy intake leading to significantly low body weight, an intense fear of weight gain, disturbance in the way body weight or shape is experienced, and limited recognition of the medical seriousness of the low weight. It often develops gradually around periods of stress, transition, or heightened self-evaluation, and is distinguished from simple dieting or medical weight loss by the fear-driven restriction and overvaluation of weight or shape.

patient.stressor_event: Death of a close family member
patient.stressor: When Audrey’s older sister died, the loss disrupted the quiet routines that had anchored her separated life: shared book-club notes, planned museum visits, and yearly hiking itineraries. In the months afterward, she turned to increasingly exact food planning and recipe tracking, initially framed as a rational project in health and order, but the restriction continued until her weight fell below what was medically appropriate for her age and build. Even as the numbers changed, she treated the low weight as a successful optimization and felt strongly that regaining weight would undermine the composure she was trying to rebuild. She eventually sought help herself through her primary-care system after a routine visit and lab follow-up led her physician to recommend psychiatric evaluation, which Audrey accepted mainly as another problem to analyze rather than because she recognized the seriousness of her weight.

S043.name: Restrictive_Intake
S043.description: Persistent restriction of energy intake relative to requirements, leading to significantly low body weight.
S043.manifestation: I came in because my doctor seems concerned that my meal planning has gotten too tight, though to me it just feels like keeping breakfast to yogurt, skipping lunch if I’m busy, and making a very measured dinner so the day stays orderly.

S044.name: Low_Weight
S044.description: A body weight that is significantly below the minimum level of health for age, sex, developmental trajectory, and physical health.
S044.manifestation: My weight has drifted down more than my doctor likes, but when I look at the chart I still find myself thinking a little lower would be a cleaner, more manageable number.

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.
S045.manifestation: If the scale is up even a pound after a normal dinner or a restaurant meal, I feel this sharp panic that I’ve lost control and need to correct it the next day.

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.
S046.manifestation: I know I’m an older woman and not trying to look young, but I still judge how well I’m handling myself by whether my waist and hips look contained in my clothes.

S084.name: Low_Weight_Severity_Non_Recognition
S084.description: Persistent lack of recognition of the seriousness of the current low body weight.
S084.manifestation: When my physician talks about my weight being medically unsafe, part of me thinks she’s overstating it because I’m still working, running my errands, and managing my own life.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: I still keep up with my analysis work and errands, but I’ve mostly stopped joining friends for meals after book club because it throws off the plan I rely on.
